name: Heuristics Report
description_text:
Perform an analysis using ONE OF the following use cases:  

Apply for a job as a Barista hosted on Indeed with a saved resume:  
https://www.indeed.com

Create a Stock Ticker watchlist on MSN 
https://www.msn.com/

Order a touchscreen laptop on Dell
http://www.dell.com/

Grocery shopping on Amazon 
https://www.amazon.com/fmc/learn-more?ref_=nav_cs_groceries

Choose your own. 
Select a site or application that has a number of issues in completing tasks or flaws in its ease of use.

Complete each of the 3 categories from any one of the use cases using the attached Template: 

Heuristics Report Template-1.docx

Situational Awareness (6 entries)

Support Mental Models (5 entries)

Support User Goals (5 entries)

You can use any combination of use cases from any site listed above to complete each category. (e.g. Dell for Situational Awareness, Indeed for Mental Models, etc.)

Per category, identify for each line item what Heuristic you see either being successfully used or fails. Include the 10 from Heuristics, plus responsiveness and accessibility.

Refer to the lecture and Jakob Nielson's heuristic that reinforces your point of view. 

Screenshots should be showing the specific area on the page you are highlighting for your example.

Make sure you have at least one example per line item in the template.

 Use as the baseline use cases:  

Findability of specific topics a user is looking for  

Discoverability of content previously unknown to user  

How does the search and navigation assist or hinder the user

Use the attached template for marking your results. You will need to reference at least one example with an explanation for each rating score. Examples should justify why something scored well or poorly. 

 

Once you complete your analysis, provide a 2 paragraph synopsis in the intro as an overview of what you found as the overarching issue(s). You can use the sample Heuristic Report as guidance for this.

Your work will be graded on:

Accuracy of heuristic identification

Strength of evidence and explanation

Correctness and consistency of scoring

Integration of lecture concepts (situational awareness, mental models, user goals)

Clarity of writing

Quality and relevance of screenshots

Depth of synthesis in the intro

⚠ As with all assignments in this course, submissions that read as technically perfect but lacking original synthesis (e.g. verbatim ChatGPT)  may receive a deduction.

 

Reference Materials

the sample project ESD Heuristics Report.docx

10 Usability Heuristics

https://www.nngroup.com/articles/ten-usability-heuristics/

https://m3.material.io/foundations/content-design/style-guide/ux-writing-best-practices

On a Mac, (CTRL-CMD-SHFT-4) will copy what you select to the clipboard, (CMD-SHFT-4) will create a screenshot file on your desktop

On a PC, you can use the Snipping Tool found in the Utilities folder.

Have your assignment in either Microsoft Word or Google Docs. Please make sure your grammar and spelling are impeccable. 

 

   Recommended Reading: 

  Don’t Make Me Think  Chapters 6 & 7
   Laws of UX Reference Site

lecture_alignment.definition: The structural design of information environments to support usability and findability through organized, labeled, and navigable content systems.
The design of user interfaces for software and digital products, focusing on visual hierarchy, interaction patterns, and user-centered layouts.
Designing products that are usable by people with diverse abilities, following WCAG guidelines and inclusive design principles.
The practice of reducing complexity, removing unnecessary elements, and creating clear, focused experiences that help users accomplish goals efficiently.
Designing systems and processes that automate repetitive tasks, reduce manual effort, and improve efficiency through intelligent orchestration.
